newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Gold finds new gleam, up almost $10 in a day.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Gold finds new gleam, up almost $10 in a day.

text.p: The price of gold has soared almost $10 an ounce in a day, making a brisk rebound from 3-3/4 year lows to which it sank only a week ago.
Gold bullion was indicated in London on Friday afternoon close to $355 an ounce before easing slightly in volatile activity.
That compared with a Thursday fixing at $345, itself a big gain from values almost as low as $336 on February 12 at what may now prove to have been the bottom of a long slide.
An accelerated rebound by gold began on Thursday in the New York COMEX futures market.

Speculative money returned to bullion after being driven out earlier this year largely on fears that more central banks would follow recent Belgian and Dutch examples and sell from their gold reserves.
Gold has now advanced on COMEX for eight straight sessions.

"The market is acting very well..." said North American Equity Services COMEX floor trader John Geraghty. "We're seeing more shortcovering this morning as the momentum of this recovery encourages the funds to take profits".
With the dollar and stock market correcting, and physical demand for gold strong in Asia in particular, it may finally be bottoming out, some New York traders said.
Helping to fire the rally was a comment on Thursday from South African Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals that gold sales by the Belgian and Dutch central banks were unlikely to be followed by others.

Elsewhere in commodity markets on Friday, new profit-taking took some froth off the top of a rally in coffee. Oil prices weakened. Copper and aluminium were again firm with London Metal Exchange 3-months copper at an 8-1/2 month high.
London robusta coffee futures traded just below $1,650 per tonne compared with last Friday's $1,705 which was at the height of a rally that had taken coffee up about 50 percent since the end of 1996.
Traders say that stocks of coffee remain low.
In the industrial metals copper extended a rally that was triggered earlier this week, against a backdrop of tight nearby supply, by prospects that China may buy copper for its strategic stockpile.
Its advance of $100 this week to $2,374 per tonne fuelled parallel rallies in other base metals. Aluminium was stronger on Friday and testing resistance around $1,625 per tonne.
But bellwether North Sea Brent Crude Oil futures opened in London on Friday at the lowest in six months - below $20 a barrel, compared with around $25 late last year.
The slide has reflected an ample supply of crude now that the United Nations has eased its Gulf War embargo against Iraq and the arrival of warmer weather on both sides of the Atlantic.
Traders also cite news that the United Nations sanctions committee on Iraq approved deeper discounts for Iraqi crude sales to the US, according to diplomatic sources.
Chicago Board of Trade soybean and soymeal futures were sharply lower in early trade on what traders said were rumours that China cancelled 450,000 tonnes in soymeal purchases.
